headline: 6 new members join Tarique-led cabinet as portfolios are reassigned
summary: Four ministers and two state ministers took oath at Bangabhaban, with several key portfolios likely to be reassigned to new faces.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expanded the cabinet this evening, with four ministers and two state ministers taking oath at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
The oaths of office and secrecy were administered by President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir shortly after he assumed the presidency.
Senior BNP leader Abdul Moyeen Khan is likely to be appointed as the minister for local government, rural development and co-operatives (LGRD).
Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) Chairman Andaleeve Rahman Partho is expected to be appointed as the information and broadcasting minister, replacing Zahir Uddin Swapan.
BNP’s Bandarban MP Saching Prue is likely to be appointed as the minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts affairs.
Rashiduzzaman Millat is expected to be appointed as the minister for civil aviation and tourism, while Afroza Khanam Rita may be reassigned as the food minister.
Additionally, Shamim Kaiser Lincoln is likely to be appointed state minister for religious affairs, and Humaiun Kobir may be appointed state minister for foreign affairs.
caption:
Six new faces join the cabinet! 🇧🇩

Who is getting which ministry? Here are the details.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expanded the cabinet this evening, with four ministers and two state ministers taking oath at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.

The oaths of office and secrecy were administered by President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir shortly after he assumed the presidency.

Senior BNP leader Abdul Moyeen Khan is likely to be appointed as the minister for local government, rural development and co-operatives (LGRD).

Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) Chairman Andaleeve Rahman Partho is expected to be appointed as the information and broadcasting minister, replacing Zahir Uddin Swapan.

BNP’s Bandarban MP Saching Prue is likely to be appointed as the minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts affairs.

Rashiduzzaman Millat is expected to be appointed as the minister for civil aviation and tourism, while Afroza Khanam Rita may be reassigned as the food minister.

Additionally, Shamim Kaiser Lincoln is likely to be appointed state minister for religious affairs, and Humaiun Kobir may be appointed state minister for foreign affairs.

headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul [[sworn in as Bangladesh’s 23rd president]]
headline: Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as Bangladesh’s 23rd president
summary: The veteran BNP leader takes the oath of office at Bangabhaban, marking the first contested presidential election since 1991.
details: Veteran politician Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh today at Bangabhaban. Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal administered the oath at approximately 7:35pm in the Darbar Hall.
The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, and various diplomats and political leaders.
Following his swearing-in, President Mirza Fakhrul administered the oath of office to new members of the cabinet.

Mirza Fakhrul was elected by lawmakers in an indirect election yesterday, marking the first contested presidential race in the country since 1991. Previously, eight presidents between 1996 and 2023 were elected unopposed.

Born in 1948 in Thakurgaon, Fakhrul is a graduate in economics from Dhaka University and began his political career as a student activist. He later served as state minister for agriculture, civil aviation, and tourism from 2001 to 2006.

Throughout his political journey, he rose through the ranks of the BNP, serving as Secretary General until August 13 this year. During previous regimes, he was imprisoned at least 11 times, spending roughly three years in jail.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd president of Bangladesh. This marks the first contested presidential election since 1991.

Veteran politician Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh today at Bangabhaban. Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal administered the oath at approximately 7:35pm in the Darbar Hall.

The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, and various diplomats and political leaders.

Following his swearing-in, President Mirza Fakhrul administered the oath of office to new members of the cabinet.

Mirza Fakhrul was elected by lawmakers in an indirect election yesterday, marking the first contested presidential race in the country since 1991. Previously, eight presidents between 1996 and 2023 were elected unopposed.

Born in 1948 in Thakurgaon, Fakhrul is a graduate in economics from Dhaka University and began his political career as a student activist. He later served as state minister for agriculture, civil aviation, and tourism from 2001 to 2006.

Throughout his political journey, he rose through the ranks of the BNP, serving as Secretary General until August 13 this year. During previous regimes, he was imprisoned at least 11 times, spending roughly three years in jail.
